title: Evil Kaomoji ψ(｀∇´)ψ: Copy & Paste Devil and Villain Faces
meta_description: Copy and paste evil kaomoji: devil grins ψ(｀∇´)ψ and Ψ(｀▽´)Ψ, scheming smirks (≖‿≖), villain laughs (｀∀´)ﾌﾊﾊﾊ and horned emoticons like }:) and >:D.
hero_tagline: Devils with pitchforks, scheming smirks and villain laughs. Tap a wicked face to copy it.
intro: Most evil kaomoji borrow the Greek letter psi, ψ or Ψ, because its three prongs look like a devil's pitchfork. Held in both hands, as in ψ(｀∇´)ψ, it frames the face like a pair of horns as well. Slanted brows made with ｀ and ´ pull the eyes into a glare, and a wide ∇ or ▽ mouth is the grin of someone pleased with their plan. Japanese laughter sounds finish the joke: ﾌﾊﾊﾊ (fuhahaha) is the stock manga villain laugh and ｹｹｹ (kekeke) is a sneer. These suit pranks, plot twists, game trash talk and a cheeky last slice of pizza. For 😈 👿 as pictures, see the devil emoji page linked below. ಠ comes from Kannada, so a device without a font for it shows a box in its place.

sections.label: Devils
sections.intro: ψ and Ψ are the pitchfork. Lowercase reads as a small imp, capital as a bigger devil.

sections.label: Scheming
sections.intro: No horns, just the look of someone with a plan. ≖ is a half-closed eye.

sections.label: Villain Laughs
sections.intro: Each face carries a Japanese laughter sound written in half-width katakana.

sections.label: Creepy
sections.intro: Wide unblinking eyes or sharp angled ones. ◣ and ◢ make slanted villain brows.

sections.label: Emoticons
sections.intro: The sideways originals. The > is a pair of angry eyebrows; } and 3 are horns.

faq.q: Why do evil kaomoji use ψ?
faq.a: ψ (psi) is a Greek letter shaped like a three-pronged fork, so it reads as a devil's pitchfork or trident. Placed on both sides of a face, it also suggests horns.
ﾌﾊﾊﾊ is fuhahaha written in half-width katakana. It is the laugh manga and anime give to villains, a slow, booming laugh rather than a giggle.
It is a sideways devil face: the curly bracket is a pair of horns above the eyes. 3:) is the same idea, and >:) swaps the horns for angry eyebrows.
